# Generator-shortcuts answer — 44e865b6a43e

Assignment: `review-0367f02076a54545`; question `generator-shortcuts`, version 1.

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed generator emits such cases.

## Answer and source binding

The strongest verified rival is **nearest equal-height association**. It fits all three canonical demonstrations and the labeled canonical test, and it agreed with all 360 inspected baseline production outputs. A lawful case with equal first and interior bar heights distinguishes it from the intended independent rotations. The repaired generator deliberately emits these distinguishing cases in every difficulty band. This is an executable structural rival; it does not memorize complete grids, color identities, or canonical dimensions. Its fit does not establish that any particular learner would choose it.

The comparison binds these selected generator sources:

| Source | Version | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline | `2.0.0` | `0a61a0c780bc44a0e01741ab8c133f6d0fb43af7b5d3eea5ef67a9c142988a3f` |
| Repaired | `2.1.0` | `81e85f5ea98487f80ee96ad6c2ea66501a55ad9ffeb0dca16ea4066646c25545` |

The intended rule keeps the canvas and bar columns fixed, rotates the left-to-right color list one position right, and independently rotates the height list one position left. The canonical normalized rule hash remains `de38c98a18568a2fc509a998ce7bc154fb797ff615dd7ec5367ae9d3178e2443`. Evidence: [baseline summary](checks/rotation-analysis/baseline/summary.json), [repaired summary](checks/rotation-analysis/final-v1/summary.json), and the [public production census](checks/lesson-census.summary.json).

## What the rival does, and why it survives the canonical examples

First, the rival shifts the height sequence left. It then matches the resulting equal-height shapes to original shapes by minimizing the sum of horizontal displacements, subject to a one-to-one correspondence and no stationary matches. Ties use a fixed lexicographic order. For each matched source index `j`, it uses the color from source index `j-2`, modulo the bar count. With distinct heights the source association is forced, and this gives the intended result. With repeated heights, the rival can exchange indistinguishable shape identities to avoid a long wraparound movement.

The canonical inputs do not expose that error. Their height lists are `[2,3,8,3]`, `[6,3,4]`, `[4,5,3,8,6]`, and `[10,1,4,4,5]`. Direct checks against every retained label establish four matches out of four. The old repeated-height sampler also avoided the distinction: it emitted only `[minimum, ascending distinct intermediates, minimum]`. The endpoint duplicate, together with the no-stationary-match requirement, forces the intended association. The other old families had distinct heights and therefore also forced it. Thus the defect has a structural explanation beyond the finite 360-input observation.

The rival implementation is in the selected generator and independently reproduced in [probe_rotation_rivals.py](repo/generators/44e865b6a43e/workspace/probe_rotation_rivals.py). Both versions agreed on all 391 inputs in the repaired probe.

## Exact lawful counterexample

Use a 9×9 orange canvas with bar columns `1,3,5,7`, colors `[1,2,3,4]`, and heights `[1,2,1,3]`. It passes the selected `self_check`. The following rows are exact grids: each digit represents one integer ARC cell.

Input: 9 rows × 9 columns. Output: 9 rows × 9 columns. Rival output: 9 rows × 9 columns.

**Input**

```text
777777777
777777777
777777777
777777777
777777777
777777777
777777747
777277747
717273747
```

**Canonical Racket output** — colors `[4,1,2,3]`, heights `[2,1,3,1]`.

```text
777777777
777777777
777777777
777777777
777777777
777777777
777772777
747772777
747172737
```

**Nearest-association rival output** — colors `[4,3,2,1]`, the same heights `[2,1,3,1]`.

```text
777777777
777777777
777777777
777777777
777777777
777777777
777772777
747772777
747372717
```

The two predictions differ at zero-based cells `(8,3)` and `(8,7)`. The rival preserves both the color multiset and the height multiset, so this is an object-correspondence error rather than an invalid-output trick.

The exact integer grids, acceptance result, and predictions are retained under counterexample name `interior_duplicate_on_square_canvas` in [scored_subjects.json](checks/rotation-analysis/final-v1/scored_subjects.json). The authoritative label is in the first [native Racket apply receipt](checks/rotation-analysis/final-v1/racket-labels-000.json). All labels in this probe came from the public `arcpuzzles apply --reference canonical --check-generator-domain` command, not from a Python mirror. The mirror was checked against those labels afterward. The seven recorded apply batches and the outer repaired probe completed with exit 0; [commands.json](checks/rotation-analysis/final-v1/commands.json) preserves exact commands and working directories.

## Does the repaired generator emit distinguishing cases?

Yes. The before/after production probes use the same replay recipe in each of `easy`, `medium`, and `hard`: for `i=0..119`, call `generate(seed=73000+i, sample_index=37*i+5, difficulty=band)` with no overrides. Versioned RNG means the two sources need not produce the same grids at a shared seed/index; this comparison fixes recipes, not input identity. Every one of the 360 production labels per source was executed through canonical Racket.

| Difficulty | Baseline nearest-rival refutations | Repaired nearest-rival refutations | Repaired nonminimum repeats | Repaired nonendpoint repeats | Repaired interior duplicate pairs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Easy | 0/120 | 61/120 | 40/120 | 70/120 | 4/120 |
| Medium | 0/120 | 64/120 | 47/120 | 69/120 | 6/120 |
| Hard | 0/120 | 66/120 | 46/120 | 71/120 | 5/120 |

All three repeat-support counts in the last three columns were zero in every baseline band. There were 29 repeated-height inputs per baseline band and 71 per repaired band. Exact inputs and recipes accompany both source-bound probe reports.

An immediate production reproducer is `generate(73000, 5, difficulty="medium")`: its 11×9 input has colors `[5,1,8,3]` and heights `[2,1,2,4]`. It is rectangular and its duplicated height is not the minimum. It refutes both nearest association and the independently verified square-canvas shortcut; the retained input SHA-256 is `614b887194eb5a723ff080d3eaa64e8a2734caef472dccd500546221fdc9a6e7`.

## Teaching schedule and lesson evidence

The distribution is deliberately nonuniform. Odd default indices produce rectangular four- or five-bar scenes with exactly one repeated height at positions `(0,j)`, where `2 <= j <= n-2`, and a randomized duplicated numerical rank. The true duplicate association costs `n` horizontal steps; the rival's crossed association costs `n-2`, so every such witness distinguishes them. At index `0 mod 4`, an even general draw uses a square canonical-scale canvas. Index `2 mod 4` is a general draw with the ordinary difficulty bias. General draws retain all four height families; mixed draws support every nonmonotone distinct ordering, and repeated draws support every admitted nonconstant repeat multiplicity and position arrangement. Caller overrides take precedence and may remove the default teaching witnesses.

For four consecutive, unskipped default indices, there are two witness inputs. Holding out any one as the query leaves at least one witness among three demonstrations. This explains `EXAMPLES_NEEDED=3`; it is **not** a claim that the task intrinsically needs three examples. A single rectangular version of the exact crossed-repeat example above refutes all ten declared competitors. Conversely, the retained local window at seed `73000`, difficulty `easy`, with demonstrations at indices `[0,2]` and query at index `1` demonstrates two-example ambiguity. The local window probe found 19/42 ambiguous one-demo rotations, 4/54 ambiguous two-demo rotations, and 0/60 ambiguous three-demo rotations. See [lesson_windows.json](checks/rotation-analysis/final-v1/lesson_windows.json).

The public materialized evidence is broader:

| Check | Materialized lessons | Query rotations | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 100 lessons per band, three demos and one query | 300 | 1,200 | No measured production or rotation ambiguity; no materialization/scoring errors or hook warnings |
| All four declared schedule starts in all three bands, fixed seed 0 | 12 | 48 | `complete_fixed_seed`; no measured production or rotation ambiguity or errors |

The first check contains 1,200 unique inputs. The fixed-seed enumeration contains 21 unique inputs because its sliding windows overlap; its 48 pair occurrences are not 48 independent draws. Both use ten unique rivals across fourteen declaration bindings. The tool's reporting modulus `period=6` is separate from the generator's declared schedule period 4. See [lesson-census.summary.json](checks/lesson-census.summary.json), [schedule-census.summary.json](checks/schedule-census.summary.json), and their hash-linked full reports. Actual accepted indices are retained by the public materializer; the schedule argument alone does not establish behavior after arbitrary rejections or overrides.

## Scope and other hypotheses

The other canonical-fitting rival rebuilds every output as a square with side equal to the input width. All four canonical inputs are square, so its four canonical matches are real. Rectangular teaching witnesses refute it. Eight wrong combinations of left/fixed/right color and height shifts complete the declared lesson competitors. Global color substitution was tested as a candidate and rejected: canonical demonstration color 8 would require inconsistent substitutions to 9, 2, and 4.

These results establish finite source-bound evidence against the declared rivals. They do not prove universal rule identification, model mastery, all-seed coverage, or training admission. The selected 7..12-row, 3..5-bar domain is preserved; no larger-canvas extrapolation is claimed. The separate proposed two-parameter prototype under [workspace/parametric](repo/generators/44e865b6a43e/workspace/parametric/README.md) is not part of the selected execution path. Its final [matrix-v4 report](checks/parametric/matrix-v4/private/summary.json) records nine episodes covering nine settings, 72 alternative-setting refutations, four canonical agreements, nine distinct shared-witness outputs, and 341 live Racket evaluations. Its nine public filenames are derived only from input grids. Earlier matrices predating that public-identifier correction are superseded for final prototype evidence. The final [staged task-test receipt](checks/task-tests-final/result.json) records successful execution with 64 tests and 17 subtests passed (81 JUnit results), exit 0. These remain prototype/repair checks, separate from source approval and training admission.
